question: What caused the First World War? Explain.

clusters.label: Names only the spark: the Sarajevo assassination
clusters.why_it_matters: Confuses trigger with cause. Exam questions ask 'how far was the assassination responsible?' — spark-only answers cap at low marks because they can't explain why one shooting became a world war.
quotes: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo caused the war
It started because Gavrilo Princip shot the Archduke in 1914

reteach.title: Spark vs powder keg
steps: Draw a powder keg labelled with the long-term tensions; put the assassination on top as the match.
Ask: matches fall on wet ground elsewhere in 1914 Europe — why did THIS one explode?
Students rewrite their answer with one sentence of spark + two of keg.
reteach.check_question: If Princip had missed, would Europe have stayed at peace in 1914? Use evidence.

clusters.diagnostic_question: 'The assassination caused the First World War.' How far do you agree? (Two paragraphs: trigger vs underlying causes.)

clusters.label: Recites long-term causes (MAIN) and alliance escalation
clusters.why_it_matters: Structurally correct. The exam risk is listing without linking: marks come from explaining how the causes interacted in July 1914, not from naming all four.
quotes: MAIN: militarism, alliances, imperialism and nationalism built up tension for years
Alliances meant a small Balkan crisis could not stay local, it escalated step by step

reteach.title: From list to chain
steps: Give students the July crisis as 6 event cards; they must order and arrow-link them with 'because'.
Ban the word 'and' between causes for one paragraph — force causal connectives.
Model one linked sentence together: 'Because of the alliance system, Austria's ultimatum meant…'
reteach.check_question: Write one sentence linking militarism to the speed of mobilization in July 1914.

clusters.diagnostic_question: Explain how TWO long-term causes worked together to turn the Sarajevo shooting into a European war.

clusters.label: Blames Germany alone (war guilt) without weighing others
clusters.why_it_matters: Partially evidence-based (blank cheque, Schlieffen Plan) but one-sided: ignores Austro-Hungarian and Russian choices. 'How far' questions punish single-cause verdicts.
quotes: Germany wanted a bigger empire and navy so it is mostly Germany's fault
Germany gave Austria a blank cheque and invaded Belgium, so Germany caused it

reteach.title: Prosecution and defence
steps: Split the board: evidence Germany pushed for war vs evidence others chose escalation (Russian mobilization, Austria's ultimatum).
Each student writes a verdict sentence with a qualifier: 'mainly', 'partly', 'least'.
Compare with Article 231: why did the peacemakers need a single guilty party?
reteach.check_question: Give one piece of evidence AGAINST the claim that Germany alone caused the war.

clusters.diagnostic_question: 'Germany was entirely responsible for the outbreak of war in 1914.' How far do you agree? Use the blank cheque AND one other country's actions.

unsure.why: An opinion, not a cause — needs your eyes
